title: Fourier stability and noise stability
statement: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and let $\rho\in[-1,1]$. Write $\widehat f(S)$ for its Fourier coefficient at a coordinate set $S$. The stability curve $\sum_S \rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^2$ equals the expected product $f(X)f(Y)$ when $X$ is uniform on the sign cube and, independently in each coordinate, $Y_i$ equals $X_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and $-X_i$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
